name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.229.0 — /spec:connect wires a client project to the hosted review service in one command: it creates or joins the project via Railway, stores the token in the git-ignored settings.local.json, proves the link, and writes the walkthrough block. The client now reads the stored token before the environment variable, and the mocks driver's terminal-confirm step names /spec:connect. The grounding contract's tokenEnv clause changed, so hosts owe a /spec:doctor re-stamp. 7.228.0 — The depended_on_by frontmatter field is retired: both spec templates stop emitting it and doctor's renumber remedy rewrites only the depends_on entries that name the spec. depends_on is the single home for dependency links; nothing in the pipeline ever read the back-link, and existing specs may keep their old lines. 7.227.0 — Test expiry's --apply now lands through the host's gateCommand: after writing, it runs the gate in the host root, and a red gate restores every trimmed and deleted file byte-for-byte, names the gate with its output tail, and exits 1 (--keep-on-red keeps the writes to fix forward; a host with no gateCommand gets a warning). The shared file walk skips git-ignored paths, so a built dist/ no longer changes what the sweep keeps, and the invariant keep-clause matches a script's basename as a whole name (catalog.json no longer names log.js). A dry run and an apply over the same committed tree now report the same counts in any checkout.
